posts.style: Carousel · The Sunken Fire Pit Lounge
posts.alt: The Sunken Fire Pit Lounge — 7-slide SDLR carousel
posts.caption:
The bouclé cushions get the compliments. The waterproofing membrane earns them.

A sunken lounge reads effortless — three steps down, fire in the middle, wind gone quiet. Getting there is structural work: sub-drainage designed before anything else, engineered footings behind every seat wall, membrane on the soil side, a gas line sized to the burner it feeds, and a route for a January storm to leave without a trace. That's why this feature lives in seven-figure backyards and almost nowhere else. The full build breakdown is on the site — link in bio.

The selections:
• Warming Trends CROSSFIRE burner
• limestone caps + travertine treads
• recessed riser lighting
• plaster + stone-veneer seat walls

Thinking about breaking the plane of your yard? DM "DESIGN" and we'll look at your grade.

posts.hook: A fire feature is judged in the first three seconds.
posts.caption:
The difference between a fire feature people gather around and one they glance at is almost entirely the part you never see: the burner.

We build ours around the Warming Trends CROSSFIRE — machined brass jets that pull more air per BTU, so the flame runs taller and fuller on roughly half the gas a drilled ring burns. Lifetime warranty on the brass. Key valve or electronic ignition. Fire glass, lava rock, or logs to match the architecture. We wrote up the full why — including the install details DIY builds miss — on the site, link in bio.

The selections:
• Warming Trends CROSSFIRE brass jet burner
• tumbled fire glass or lava rock media
• dedicated, permitted gas line sized to the burner
• limestone + board-formed concrete surrounds

posts.hook: A cinema you can use 300 nights a year.
posts.caption:
The marine layer rolls in around the second act. The fire takes over from there.

An outdoor cinema in San Diego earns its keep maybe 300 nights a year — per night of use, one of the most rational luxuries a backyard can hold. Ours are built as architecture: a plaster projection wall that reads as sculpture by day, speakers that vanish into the planting, seating built for a three-hour film, and lighting that dims in scenes instead of switching off. Full design guide on the site — link in bio.

The selections:
• purpose-built plaster projection wall
• FX Luminaire Luxor zoned lighting
• in-ground landscape speakers
• ventilated masonry projector cabinet
• flanking fire feature

If Friday nights deserve better than the living room, DM "DESIGN".

posts.hook: The base matters more than the paver.
posts.caption:
Two manufacturers cover most of the paver work we install — and which one goes on which project is a design decision, not a coin flip.

The rule: the material serves the house. Urbana beside Spanish Colonial. Blu 60 on coastal-contemporary. Mega-Arbel where the patio should read quarried. Industria where minimalism wants a knife-edge joint. And under every one of them: an engineered base compacted in lifts, polymeric sand, proper edge restraint. That's where the ten-year difference lives — no brochure can sell it to you. The full comparison, line by line, is on the site. Link in bio.

The selections:
• Belgard Urbana · Mega-Arbel · Dimensions
• Techo-Bloc Blu 60 · Aberdeen · Industria
• engineered compacted base + polymeric jointing

Not sure which your house wants? DM "DESIGN" and we'll match the surface to the architecture.

posts.hook: The fastest-growing estate feature is one word: recovery.
posts.caption:
Ask what's changed in estate backyard briefs over the last few years and the answer is one word: recovery.

Building the circuit properly is quiet, dense infrastructure — a dedicated electrical run for the sauna, a chiller circuit holding plunge water in the 40s, hot and cold service to a real outdoor shower, floor drains and dry wells under all of it, and honed stone that's kind to bare feet in January. It shares its bones with the rest of the yard, which is why it's a contractor's project, not a weekend delivery. Full guide on the site — link in bio.

The selections:
• Diamond Spas stainless cold plunge
• cedar sauna, glass door to the garden
• rainfall outdoor shower + teak screen
• honed limestone underfoot

posts.style: Carousel · The Turf We Actually Install
posts.alt: The Turf We Actually Install — 8-slide SDLR carousel
posts.hook: The imperfect blend is what looks expensive.
posts.caption:
The gap between turf that fools the eye and turf that reads fake from the sidewalk comes down to four spec decisions: pile height, color blend, infill, and edging — plus the base nobody sees.

We install SYNLawn and ProGreen almost exclusively: SYNLawn's plant-based backing holds fibers as well as anything we've laid; ProGreen's heavier denier takes abuse and recovers. Under both: excavation, compacted base graded for drainage, seam work that disappears. The arithmetic does the rest — no water bill, no mowing, green through every drought cycle. All four specs explained on the site, link in bio.

The selections:
• SYNLawn residential turf (plant-based backing)
• ProGreen heavy-traffic lines
• silica sand / cooling infill — never crumb rubber
• concealed steel edging

Replacing a thirsty lawn this year? DM "DESIGN" and we'll spec it for your yard.

posts.alt: FX Luminaire vs Kichler — 7-slide SDLR carousel
posts.hook: Nobody sees what fixtures cost. Only what light does.
posts.caption:
Both systems are excellent. They are not interchangeable.

Kichler's architectural line delivers roughly the same visual result as premium fixtures at 30–40% of the cost — it's our pick for most residential programs. FX Luminaire earns its premium through Luxor: zoning, dimming, and color control across an entire property, which matters on estates where the motor court, terrace, and oak canopy each want their own scene. Either way, the rules hold: 2700K throughout, fewer-but-better fixtures, conduit under the patios before they're paved. Full comparison on the site — link in bio.

The selections:
• Kichler architectural landscape line
• FX Luminaire fixtures + Luxor controller
• 2700K throughout, zoned + dimmable

Want your yard at night to match your yard at noon? DM "DESIGN".

posts.hook: Water's most expensive job isn't holding swimmers.
posts.caption:
The most expensive thing water can do in a backyard is not hold swimmers. It is hold attention.

A wall of moving water replaces the neighbor's traffic with white noise. A mirror pool doubles the house at dusk — the estate's most expensive photograph and its cheapest one to take. A rain curtain turns a pergola bay into a threshold. All of it runs on millimeter-level tolerances and machinery you'll never see. The full anatomy of all three features is on the site — link in bio.

The selections:
• dark granite / board-formed concrete water wall
• bronze-spillway rain curtain
• dark-bottom mirror pool, flush edges
• concealed recirculation vault + filtration

Which one does your terrace want? DM "DESIGN".

posts.hook: A fixed roof decides once. This one decides daily.
posts.caption:
A fixed pergola makes you choose between sun and shelter at the design meeting. A louvered one lets you choose every afternoon.

StruXure's Pergola X is the spec when the patio is a genuine room — outdoor kitchen, dining terrace, TV wall — and weather ending the evening is an actual cost. Extruded aluminum that ignores salt air, louvers to 170°, gutters concealed in the frame, lighting and heat designed in rather than clamped on. Engineered and permitted like any roof, because it is one. And where the architecture wants timber, we'll say so — we build both. Full review on the site, link in bio.

The selections:
• StruXure Pergola X louvered roof
• integrated LED lighting + heaters
• concealed frame-and-post gutter system
• rain-sensor automation

Want the roof that thinks? DM "DESIGN".

The differentiator isn't a more expensive grill. It's fire in multiple forms, under a real roof.

A chef-grade pavilion is four trades working in sequence: masonry for an oven that will never move again, gas plumbed and sized per appliance, ventilation planned into the ceiling, counters engineered like a working line. Wood for the ninety-second pizza and the Sunday bread. Gas for Tuesday. The gaucho grill for the night nobody wants to end — everyone standing around the dying embers, unwilling to go inside. posts.hook: A grill review from people who set them in stone.
posts.caption:
We don't review grills we haven't set into stone. The Summerset Sizzler Pro is the one we spec most in the professional middle tier — the most hardware per dollar between the big-box boxes that rust through in three seasons and the badges you pay for at the top.

Four cast stainless burners, 56,000 BTUs over 740 square inches, ceramic briquettes for even heat, a rear infrared rotisserie clients think they won't use and then use every week. 443-grade steel that shrugs at the marine layer. Lifetime warranty on the parts that matter. Full installer's review on the site — link in bio. Not sponsored; we spec what holds up.

The selections:
• Summerset Sizzler Pro 32" (natural gas, plumbed + permitted)
• masonry island, insulated jacket where framed
• limestone counters, ventilation to spec

Planning an island around it? DM "DESIGN".

posts.hook: The feature golfers use every single day.
posts.caption:
Twenty minutes with a wedge before dinner. A putting contest after it.

Of all the estate features we build, the short-game complex has the highest use-per-dollar of anything in the yard — because golfers don't need an occasion. The version that earns daily use is built like real golf: contour shaped into the base itself, a fringe that takes a chip and holds it, a bunker that makes low-handicap visitors laugh out loud, and drainage that never puddles the low read. The full build guide is on the site — link in bio.

The selections:
• SYNLawn Golf putting surface
• contoured, compacted sub-base
• dedicated chipping tee pad
• lined + drained practice bunker
• glare-free low lighting

The most impressive technology in a seven-figure backyard is the technology you cannot see.

One touch: path lights rise, the louvers tilt against the low sun, the water wall wakes, music comes from nowhere, the pool shifts to its evening color. Not eleven apps — one intention. It only works because the conduit went in while the ground was open, which is why automation is a construction decision, not a gadget purchase. The full playbook is on the site — link in bio.

posts.alt: The Estate Sport Court — 7-slide SDLR carousel
posts.hook: Sport courts are, by default, ugly. Ours aren't.
posts.caption:
The hard part of a backyard court isn't the court. It's building one that doesn't erase the garden around it.

That takes a post-tensioned slab laser-graded to sport tolerances, surfacing in estate colors instead of municipal green, black steel fencing planted with jasmine where chain-link would've gone, and the smartest move of all — cutting the court a half-level below the terrace so it disappears until someone suggests a game. Regulation pickleball with true run-off wants roughly 30 by 60 feet; tighter lots get a multi-sport pad. Full guide on the site — link in bio.

The selections:
• VersaCourt / SnapSports surfacing
• post-tensioned, laser-graded slab
• black powder-coated steel fencing + star jasmine
• zoned, shielded LED court lighting

Ready for home-court advantage? DM "DESIGN".

posts.hook: The most-used room isn't inside the house.
posts.caption:
Every estate has a most-used room. On properties with a great pool house, it's rarely inside the main residence.

Glass walls pocket away and the conditioned room becomes an open pavilion — coffee at seven, towels at noon, a fire and a film after dark. The full bath is what changes how visiting family experiences a week at the property. And because it touches grading, utilities, hardscape, pool, and planting at once, it's drawn first — the anchor of the remodel, not an afterthought. The full guide is on the site — link in bio.

The selections:
• full-height pocketing glass walls, flush thresholds
• kitchenette + under-counter refrigeration
• full bath with outdoor shower access
• wood ceiling, extended shade roofline
• fireplace for the winter half of the calendar
